messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: INFER-CPU-QUEUE-OVERFLOW fired for service=redwood-inference-hosted, region=us-west1, queue_depth=9850, autoscaler_lag=35m. Escalation level: page -> on-call.
pagerduty: Page sent to sam (primary on-call). Incident link: https://pd.example/INC12345
sam: acked. jumping in, pulling logs now. seeing repeated `ProvisionerError: nodepool quota exceeded` in node-provisioner logs.
devon: copying logs — looks like the autoscaler requested nodes but cloud provider returned RATE_LIMITED on spot pool. also many warmup jobs stuck.
priya: customer impact check — embedding latency spikes to 5-12s for hosted customers in us-west1, error rate 0.8% on generation requests.
sam: ok plan: 1) temporarily increase fallback capacity to dedicated-warmpool-1 (manual attach) 2) spin up hot nodes from on-demand 3) re-route small customers to us-east1 for reads. anyone can take manual spin? ops-jen if you can help with cloud console?
ops-jen: on it — starting manual hot node allocation, creating a nodepool on-demand with 4 x n2-standard-16. I'll annotate steps here.
ops-jen: ran:

```
gcloud container node-pools create hot-now \
  --cluster=infra-us-west1 \
  --machine-type=n2-standard-16 \
  --num-nodes=4 \
  --labels=purpose=hotpool,ephemeral=true
```
ops-jen: nodes are provisioning, ETA ~3m. also bumped autoscaler max nodes to 120 for the inference cell (was 80).
devon: nice. while nodes spin, we should reduce batch sizes on live routed workloads to reduce queue pressure — updating router config (canary first).
priya: started customer reroutes to us-east1 for non-low-latency SLAs. Monitoring impact.
sam: temporary mitigations in place: manual nodes requested + routing. next steps: investigate why autoscaler didn't request on-demand fallback earlier — look at policy for spot->ondemand fallback threshold.
maria: I see heartbeat gap between autoscaler-controller and cloudprovider adapter at 00:12 UTC — controller logs show backoff retries and then cached quota response. pushing a hotfix to reduce backoff.
devon: if autoscaler policy had allowed `fallback_policy: immediate_on_deny` we might've avoided manual spin. will raise PR after incident.
incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty escalation level advanced to SEV2 at 00:20 UTC due to customer latency impact.
sam: status update: new nodes joined, kube-scheduler placing pods on hot nodes. queue depth down from 9850 -> 1200 in 6m. error rate dropping. good.
ops-jen: finished attaching warm cache pool + warmed KV prefixes for top-10 customers.
priya: embedding latency 95perc now back to ~220ms for rerouted traffic; overall 95perc for us-west1 trending down to 700ms.
sam: still watching. keep throttling large batch jobs and prioritize small interactive requests.
maria: opened issue INF-1829 to track autoscaler backoff bug and add metrics for provider-denied node requests.
devon: filing PR for policy change: add immediate on-demand fallback + a short-circuit when spot failure rate > 5% in a 5m window.
sam: handoff: I'm staying 30m for post-mitigation; if anything regresses escalate to ops-sre. tagging @devon for implementation and @maria for controller fix.
pagerduty: sam acknowledged at 00:24 UTC. Incident assigned to sam, devon, maria.
priya: thanks team — I'll notify impacted customers via status page and include mitigation summary.
sam: confirmed: last check queue_depth=180, autoscaler back to healthy view after nodes joined. closing alert watch, will convert to follow-up ticket.
incident-bot: Incident note: page closed by sam at 00:34 UTC. Follow-ups: INF-1829 (autoscaler backoff), INF-1830 (routing playbook updates), INF-1831 (on-call runbook: manual hot node steps).
sam: closing thread here. great work. :thumbsup:
